doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Miles Davis's phone call and the invitation to the Village Vanguard
summary: Miles tracked her down at her mother-in-law's and invited her to open for him; he refused to play unless she opened.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: With that in mind then, what was your reasoning for accepting Miles Davis‘ invitation, when he called you and invited you to perform with him at the Village Vanguard?
If Miles Davis had called you and asked you, okay, okay? The way it came about, because I‘d been loving him all my life, you know.
Had you ever encountered him before when you were in East St. Louis?

No, I encountered his wife. I‘m not talking about that. It was crazy, and I was in . . . just like you heard about it. Maybe you‘ve read it or something, you know. I‘m down in the country with my mother-in-law, and I went to the phone. [imitates voice] ―I want you to come in the August, somebody, a lot of people I think you ought to meet.‖ And I laughed, you know. That was it. But somebody said to me, ―No, this was not a joke. This was Miles.‖ And to this day I don‘t know how he found out where I was. So I went to New York and then, you know, that was the beginning. And he‘s my love. I loved him with a passion. Anyway, he let me know that everything was cool. It wasn‘t no b.s., you know. He had little young boys, then. They all sang one of the songs off that first album I did.

And I said, ―I don‘t believe it.‖ I stood there and I cried, you know, and I met a lot of people with him. That one time, I didn‘t know who they were, and who Gil Evans was, and Bill Evans and a whole bunch of those other people. But anyway, and then when he said he told Max Gordon, ―I‘m not going to play unless she opens.‖ Yeah. That was something. It knocked me down. My sweet love.
